decisions.decision: A venture's customer problems are a hierarchy, held in the forms of its problem record and ranked on every read. Two relations hold the tree, and they are different claims: parent, which says a problem is a narrower case of another, after Teresa Torres's opportunity solution tree, and cause_of, which says a problem is a cause of another, after problem tree analysis in the Logical Framework Approach. One problem per ICP profile is its core problem, named by a single field on the profile, and one form at a time carries the status target, the problem being worked on now; both records are gated, so only a person settles either. The evidence is counted, never scored: each validation interview codes the problems it bears on with raised unprompted, ranked first and pays for a workaround, and a problem's priority is the weighted sum of those counts, with the weights unvalidated priors in packages/naive/src/functions/strategy/problem-priority.json that a venture replaces under problems in naive.config.json with the person who set them. Primary, secondary and tertiary are labels on the computed order and are never stored; before any interview has coded a problem the order is the founder's own, the order the forms are listed in, and the output labels that basis a hypothesis. A fail-closed rule holds the venture to the problem it says it is solving: no solution, offer or public content while the venture has no problem tree, no form is the target, or the primary profile names no core problem. The customer's problems live here and the business's own do not: those are decisions, seams and handoffs. Every new field is optional, so a record written before this decision is a one-problem tree and stays valid with no migration.
decisions.why: Torian decided this on 2026-11-26: add all of the problems and a hierarchy over them, a primary, a secondary and tertiary problems or some other method, by the best practices and the standards, and cover his blind spots. He accepted the design the same day with the record it had to hold: a core problem, doesn't know what to do next, with one cause and one narrower case under it. Two standards already answer the shape, so Naive uses both rather than coining one (EE-014), and keeping cause apart from narrower case is what makes the tree say anything. Priority is computed because a stored rank drifts from the evidence, and the weights are data because what counts as evidence of a problem is a judgment a venture owns. The fail-closed rule is a check today; the refusal at the write belongs on the general requires mechanism rather than a second bespoke gate hook.

decisions.decision: The work has an order, and the order is enforced. Each function workflow says in requires what must exist before anyone may run it, in three kinds and no others: records, routes whose record is live in the venture; meetings, a function workflow a meeting walked and closed with its goal reached (EE-200); and decisions, ids a person has decided. A step may add entries of its own. It fails closed: an entry that cannot be resolved, for any reason, counts as missing, so a workflow whose ground is unknown does not run, and a draft the gate holds is not live, so an agent cannot settle its own prerequisite. prerequisitesOf(dir, "<function>/<workflow>", step) in packages/naive/src/engine/prerequisites.ts is the one verdict every caller reads, { met, missing }, each missing entry with its kind, ref, why and state. The lock holds people as well as agents: naive due marks a blocked workflow blocked, naive loop starts nothing whatever the mode, naive agent run --workflow refuses it, and the router refuses a write to a route that only blocked workflows write, for an agent and a person alike, naming what unblocks it first. decisions/* and operations/handoff are never locked, so the answer to a lock is always reachable, and the rule is scoped to the functions the venture lists. A person may pass mentura <route> write --override --by <person> --why <text>, and the provenance line keeps the rule, the person, the reason and the missing list; an agent never may. The chain Naive ships is data in the workflow files, not code: the strategy foundation before products, products before what is sold, and strategy/intake the root that waits on nothing. A venture loosens or tightens an entry under prerequisites in naive.config.json, which the schema holds to set_by a person, so only a person ever opens a lock. naive blocked lists the venture's workflows in phase, function and workflow order with what unblocks each first.
decisions.why: Torian, 2026-11-26: a fail-closed system on many activities, a hierarchical workflow that is highly opinionated and actually locks you out from doing certain things until others are done, such as the strategy and the foundational records that must exist first, blocking people as well as agents from starting or completing work until they have held certain meetings, each meeting drafting durable objects. The order of the work was already implicit in the function modules, read by need-now and the phase gates as advice, so nothing stopped a product card being written before anyone knew who it was for. Making the chain data in the workflows keeps it contextual: it is read, checked and overridden, never hard-coded, and the override is a person's alone because a lock an agent can open is no lock.

decisions.decision: A pre-registration is a durable object of the strategy function, and it comes before the mission, the vision and the other strategy documents. The record type pre-registration (route foundation/pre-registration/[id], owned by strategy, suggested from Discovery) holds a thesis written so it can fail, the assumptions under it with how critical and how uncertain each is, the method (who, how many, how recruited, what is asked or observed), the measures each with a threshold and the date it is judged by, what does not count as evidence, and the action on a pass and on a fail. A person registers it. From registration on the thesis, assumptions, method, measures, thresholds, judged-by dates, exclusions, decision rules and who registered it when never change, for a person either: a departure is appended to deviations with the date, what changed, why and who, and a real change is a new pre-registration that supersedes the old one with a reason, so both what was promised and what happened stay readable. A verdict is written once and is a person's; a measure's pass or fail is its observed value against its registered threshold, which is arithmetic. Naive ships no threshold and no sample size: each is the venture's own, asked for or raised as a strategy-or-constitution decision, and the shipped template labels every number in it an example. Two layers hold the freeze: packages/naive/src/engine/pre-registration.ts is the pure rule the router applies to every write, and packages/naive/src/checks/check-pre-registration.ts compares each registered field with the version in the venture's blob store, which catches a hand edit that never went through the router. Blobs are not backfilled, so a record registered before the blob store existed is reported unverifiable and does not fail.
decisions.why: Torian decided this on 2026-11-26: add pre-registration into the workflow as one of the durable objects that comes before another set of durable objects such as mission statement, vision and other strategy docs, with the record frozen once a person approves it (claim, assumptions, measures, thresholds, dates and decision rules), deviations appended beside it rather than edited into it, and a full supersede to a new version allowed with a reason. A mission and a vision written before anything has been tested are claims nobody can lose an argument with, because the standard of proof is then set after the evidence arrives. The practice and its words are standard: preregistration in science (Nosek et al. 2018), discovery-driven planning's assumption checklist and milestones (McGrath and MacMillan 1995), the Test Card's metric and criterion (Bland and Osterwalder 2019), and HARKing (Kerr 1998) for why the exclusions are fixed in advance.

decisions.decision: A strategic claim is written the way a requirement is written, and it is a record. The record type bet (route foundation/bets/[id], owned by the strategy function, decision class strategy-or-constitution, suggested from Discovery) holds one claim of one kind: empirical, forecast, causal, premise, or selection-rule. A claim names its population with what is left in and out, its measure, its comparator, its threshold, the date it is judged on, the source the value is read from and, when it is tested by counting cases, the denominator; statementForm renders the fixed sentence for the kind from those parts, after EARS, so the parts are what is written and the sentence is rendered beside the founder's own wording for them to confirm. A selection rule says whom the venture backs and whom it does not, with an observable test; it is a value, not a claim, so it is never resolved by evidence and never scored. Every bet says what would show it wrong, names the premises it rests on as bets of kind premise with their own ids, and names at least one rival with the observation that would tell the two apart. Evidence is appended for and against and is never removed, and a bet reported supported while a premise of it is refuted is an error. A person registers a bet, a person alone puts odds on it with who set them and what they had already seen from the OSF template's five answers, and a person alone resolves it; an agent's write of a status, a probability, a resolution or the registration fields is refused before the gate and the refusal names the person's command. Naive ships no line, no date and no probability: each is the founder's, asked for or raised as a strategy-or-constitution decision. From registration on the claim never changes, for a person either: a narrowed or corrected claim is a new bet whose supersedes names the old one with a reason, so the old claim and its outcome stay readable. A registered pre-registration (EE-220) that names a bet in its tests freezes that bet's claim even while the bet is still proposed, so a claim cannot be widened after the search starts. The freeze is held in two layers as the pre-registration's is: packages/naive/src/engine/bets.ts is the pure rule the router applies to every write, and packages/naive/src/checks/check-bets.ts compares each frozen field with the version in the venture's blob store, which catches a hand edit that never went through the router, and reports a bet registered before the blob store existed as unverifiable rather than failed. The one contradiction a machine settles is two registered lines over the same population, measure, unit and date that cannot both hold; whether a claim is true is evidence and a person's judgment, and the register is never called verified or proved. Attacking a bet is premise-lint's work, not a new linter: bets are a sixth kind in packages/naive/src/checks/premise-lint.ts with one new aspect, no-counter-evidence, for a claim with no evidence against it and no rival. A resolved forecast is scored with its prior by the Brier score, because every later probability saw the evidence; a mixed or unresolvable outcome is not scored rather than guessed at, and a bet the venture is working to make true carries intends_to_cause and is reported apart and never as foresight.
decisions.why: Torian decided this on 2026-11-26: create a list of bets similar to how we would create system requirements, a bet being the same thing for strategy, with a research flow for testing them, and we would have to try to disprove our bets and attack the premise of our bets, which is the pre-registration's purpose, plus skills for writing them and lints over the writing. A strategy written as prose cannot be wrong, because nothing in it says what would count against it. The practice and its words are standard: the characteristics of one requirement (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018) and a fixed sentence template per kind (Mavin et al., EARS, 2009) for how a claim is written; Popper (1959) for the counter-observation and Duke (Quit, 2022) for pairing it with a date; Dewar (Assumption-Based Planning, 2002) and Toulmin (1958) for the premises a claim rests on; Platt (strong inference, 1964) for the rival and the test that tells them apart; Heuer (1999) for evidence against deciding; Nosek et al. (PNAS 2018) and the OSF Preregistration template for keeping prediction apart from postdiction and for the five answers to what had already been seen; and Tetlock and Gardner (2015) with Brier (1950) for a probability, a date and a score afterwards. The mechanism is what Naive ships: no bet of the founder's is shipped as content, and no number in one is an agent's.

decisions.decision: Naive is tested by simulating businesses end to end. A simulator in packages/simulate/, outside the package's files so it never ships, drives Naive's real router, gate, loop and function agents against a seeded world of synthetic customers, competitors, money and simulated tools, with simulated people answering every decision. Three invented seed businesses together reach all 13 functions and all five phases: a solo founder in Discovery, an existing service business onboarded at Beachhead, and a seven-year physical-product run to Platform. Every simulated record carries the synthetic-record label (EE-198), and only a simulation flag, refused outside a simulation folder, lets a gate grade synthetic evidence. Lean proves the lifecycle rules in packages/naive/lean/Naive/Lifecycle.lean, and each run's trace is exported as cases lake build checks. Design: docs/design/SIMULATION_2026-11-26.md. Nothing is built yet.
decisions.why: Torian on 2026-11-26 attacked the premise of starting with solo founders: testing only there leaves ten of the 13 functions and four of the five phases unrun, and existing businesses are where onboarding and the source-of-truth matrix meet real data. He asked to simulate long-running businesses on the platform, verify formally that the process holds across functions, phases and tools, and later demo the runs. Open simulators (YC-Bench, CEO-Bench) cover parts of one company and are Python, so their designs are rewritten in TypeScript on Effect.

decisions.decision: A product's capabilities are records. product-capability.schema.json is one capability, or a category of capabilities, at <venture>/product/capabilities/<id>.json (route product/capabilities/[id]), in the purpose layer with function products and data master: a name, the product it belongs to, its kind, its parent category (null for a category directly under the products function; a capability always has one), the agent role that owns it and its status, live, building or retired. check-ventures.ts checks the tree across files: the product exists, the parent is a category of the same product, categories form no loop, and nothing under a retired category is live or building. An app reads the records to staff a capability agent (<capability>-agent) and its category agent, and to give a site or docs container its owner. Naive starts no agent and enforces no container: that stays in the app.
decisions.why: Torian on 2026-11-26 asked for one agent per capability (time travel, for example), with category agents holding authority over their group, each owning the containers of the marketing site and docs that describe it. Mentura's site agents (containers.json) need a source for which capabilities exist, who owns each and whether it is still live; product.schema.json has features with no owner, status or hierarchy. A record keeps that in the business's own store, with provenance, instead of in an app's config.

decisions.decision: Every instruction file Naive writes says that existing code wins over stale documentation. The sentence is CODE_OVER_DOCS in packages/naive/src/core/code-over-docs.ts, word for word from Xu and Wu (2026): when a repository's documentation and its existing code disagree, follow the conventions used in the existing code and name each inconsistency in the final reply. init-venture and naive dev write it into a venture's AGENTS.md, workspace.ts into the workspace's, and the Claude Code and Cursor adapters into their entry files; Codex reads it in AGENTS.md. A venture created before this gets it only when someone adds the line (no migration, not built).
decisions.why: Xu and Wu (2026, arXiv 2610.30571) found that coding agents followed a stale AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md over the existing code in 90% of choices, even when they named the conflict, because the file reaches the model as an instruction and the code only as tool output; Codex rewrote working code to match the file and broke its tests. The one sentence, given as an instruction, moved 91% of choices to the code and stopped the rewrites. Torian on 2026-11-27: "This is the fix I've been trying to make for so long. The documentations are always wrong and never being properly updated."

decisions.decision: Every element of APQC's PCF 8.0 is covered by its function's module, and a check says which are not. A level 3 process is covered by one workflow of the module whose optional `process` field names it, with one step per level 4 activity under it, each naming the activity; a level 2 process group by one skill whose SKILL.md frontmatter names it as `process_group`; a category by a module with an agent and a workflow. A level 5 task is never a step of its own and is counted under its covered activity. packages/naive/src/checks/check-pcf-coverage.ts reports coverage per level and per category, lists the gaps with --gaps, fails on a claim with the wrong structure, and fails on any gap with --complete. The process workflows run on request and wait on their function's intake meeting.
decisions.why: Torian asked long ago for every PCF element to be audited and given detailed skills and workflows. On 2026-11-27 the 35 shipped workflows touched 6 of 1,352 activities and no process or process group, and no check made the gap visible. Torian on 2026-11-27: "that work needs to be done and it needs to be done immediately."

decisions.decision: An agent's word that it finished a step is not evidence. A function workflow run carries a package, one result per step (done, not-needed, nothing-to-record or skipped), and a done step's evidence is the provenance lines it wrote under its own session run:<run>/<step>. packages/naive/src/engine/run-proof.ts verifies each line against the venture's hash-chained provenance log and blob store: the session, the runner's role or a specialist of its function, the step's time window, a route the step may write through the router, and the bytes kept. Only a step with consider may be judged not needed, and only a step whose writes are all decisions/* may have nothing to record, each with a reason. `naive workflow run` runs each step as a durable Effect workflow activity and gathers the evidence itself. The skipped ledger keeps every step a run does not prove, check-runs.ts fails when a workflow's latest run does not verify, and the lifecycle gate refuses a phase change until the phase's gate records match their last recorded write, its latest runs verify and its intakes are walked, unless a person overrides with a reason.
decisions.why: Torian, 2026-11-27: "We don't want to take agents at their word for having completed a step. We want to be able to verify and for them to be able to prove that their work was completed." And: a venture must be able to prove it exited Discovery by proving its prerequisite records exist. Before this, a run was a line that said done, and a phase gate counted any file at a record's path.

decisions.decision: Evidence can record a test of a physical thing: the unit tested by serial (subject.article), the conditions the run happened under, and each result's measured values, each a quantity, a number, a UCUM unit code and an optional limit. A result cannot pass with a measured value outside its limit; check-execution.mjs refuses it.
decisions.why: Torian, 2026-11-19 05:03Z on a decision card in the Everything Ecosystem redesign, before the SpaceX study: the study asks what counts as evidence (a test flight, a static fire, a simulation), and evidence could say a product passed but not which unit was tested, under what conditions, or what was measured.
